data.why: The repository bundles data/sample_batch.csv, which the Streamlit batch-screening page itself reads and offers as a download button, and includes an invalid formula and a duplicate composition row the tool is meant to flag.

goals: Screen a single chemical composition (e.g. LiFePO4) to get a calibrated stability probability, predictive uncertainty, OOD risk, and candidate score
Upload a CSV batch of candidate compositions and run screening to produce a ranked, scored list
Filter and sort the ranked batch by predicted stability, review flag, probability, uncertainty, and OOD risk to prioritize candidates
Export the ranked screening results as CSV or JSON for downstream use
Review past screening runs stored in history
Read the model card to understand model design, training data, evaluation metrics, and limitations

review.summary: The tree matches the README's stated purpose: calibrated stability probability, uncertainty, OOD risk and a candidate score for one formula or a CSV batch, then filtering, export and history. It covers every control in the Streamlit UI, and all 12 screenshots I sampled show what their nodes say. The remaining gaps are paths the sample data could not reach (flagged batch rows, malformed files) and a missing model-card feature, both small enough to file the tree as is.
